[[EuroCup Basketball|EuroCup]] | team = PAOK Thessaloniki | number = 12 | birth_date = {{birth date and age|1999|3|23}} | birth_place = [[Manhattan, Kansas]], U.S. | high_school = [[Manhattan High School|Manhattan]] (Manhattan, Kansas) | college = [[Northwest Missouri State Bearcats men's basketball|Northwest Missouri State]] (2018–2022) | draft_year = 2022 | career_start = 2022 | years1 = {{nbay|2022|full=y}} | team1 = [[Houston Rockets]] | years2 = [[2022–23 NBA G League season|2022–2023]] | team2 = →[[Rio Grande Valley Vipers]] | years3 = 2023–2026 | team3 = [[Le Mans Sarthe Basket|Le Mans]] | years4 = 2026–present | team4 = [[PAOK BC|PAOK Thessaloniki]] | highlights = * 2× All-[[LNB Élite]] Second Team ([[2024–25 LNB Élite season|2025]], [[2025–26 LNB Élite season|2026]]) * [[Leaders Cup|French League Cup]] winner ([[2025 Pro A Leaders Cup|2025]]) * [[Leaders Cup|French League Cup]] MVP (2025) * 3× [[NCAA Division II men's basketball tournament|NCAA Division II champion]] ([[2019 NCAA Division II men's basketball tournament|2019]], [[2021 NCAA Division II men's basketball tournament|2021]], [[2022 NCAA Division II men's basketball tournament|2022]]) * 2× NCAA Division II Tournament MOP (2019, 2022) * 2× [[NABC Player of the Year|NABC Division II Player of the Year]] (2021, 2022) * [[Bevo Francis Award]] winner (2022) * 2× First-team Division II All-American – [[National Association of Basketball Coaches|NABC]], D2CCA (2021, 2022) * 3× [[Mid-America Intercollegiate Athletics Association|MIAA]] Player of the Year (2020–2022) * 4× First-team All-MIAA (2019–2022) * MIAA Freshman of the Year (2019) }} '''Trevor Hudgins''' (born March 23, 1999) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for [[PAOK BC|PAOK Thessaloniki]] of the [[Greek Basketball League]] (GBL) and the [[EuroCup Basketball|EuroCup]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Northwest Missouri State Bearcats men's basketball|Northwest Missouri State Bearcats]] where he led the team to three consecutive [[NCAA Division II men's basketball tournament|NCAA Division II championships]]. Hudgins was named as the [[NABC Player of the Year|NABC Division II Player of the Year]] in 2021 and 2022 and the [[Mid-America Intercollegiate Athletics Association]] (MIAA) Player of the Year from 2020 to 2022, making him one of the most decorated players in [[NCAA Division II]] history. Hudgins started his professional career during the 2022–23 season with the [[Houston Rockets]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] ([[NBA]]), on a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Rio Grande Valley Vipers]] of the [[NBA G League]]. He joined [[Le Mans Sarthe Basket|Le Mans]] in 2023. ==Early life== Hudgins is the son of Sterling and Pat Hudgins.{{cite web |last1=Roush |first1=Chris |title=For the love of the game |url=https://www.kq2.com/news/top-stories/for-the-love-of-the-game/article_0684bcd0-ab85-11ec-a787-9f2a940bb996.html |website=KQ2 |access-date=June 28, 2022 |date=March 24, 2022}} His father is a pastor.{{cite web |last1=Echlin |first1=Greg |title=No border rivalry here: A Kansas native fuels a Missouri team's national title hopes |url=https://www.hppr.org/hppr-news/2022-03-14/no-border-rivalry-here-a-kansas-native-fuels-a-missouri-teams-national-title-hopes |website=High Plains Public Radio |access-date=June 28, 2022 |date=March 14, 2022}} Hudgins had his beginnings in basketball by playing with a ball when he was old enough to walk. He also participated in [[American football|football]], [[Association football|soccer]], [[bowling]], [[golf]] and [[Pool (cue sports)|pool]] while growing up. ==High school career== Hudgins attended [[Manhattan High School]] in his hometown of [[Manhattan, Kansas]]. The basketball team's head coach was relieved of his duties during Hudgins' freshman season and replaced by Benji George. George allowed Hudgins to play on the varsity team during the latter half of the season and recognised that he would take over the team's [[point guard]] position with his distribution abilities. In his sophomore season, Hudgins helped the team improve to a 18–3 record and a championship in the Centennial League. He had played with a pass-first approach and shunned scoring until encouraged by the coaching staff. Hudgins led the team to a second Centennial League title as a junior and was named the conference's player of the year. He earned a second consecutive conference player of the year award as he led the team to a third Centennial League title in his senior season.{{cite web |last1=Watkins |first1=Jimmy |title=Former MHS star Trevor Hudgins wins conference POY for 2nd straight season |url=https://themercury.com/sports/former-mhs-star-trevor-hudgins-wins-conference-poy-for-2nd-straight-season/article_cc332a01-2af6-5598-bea2-b602be88b1d4.html |website=The Mercury |access-date=July 4, 2021 |date=March 3, 2021}}{{cite web |last1=Collins |first1=Sean |title=Former Manhattan High basketball star reflects on college title |url=https://themercury.com/sports/former-manhattan-high-basketball-star-reflects-on-college-title/article_471a3c31-dcb3-5080-83a0-e9382f844d35.html |website=The Mercury |access-date=July 4, 2021 |date=August 18, 2019}} ===College recruiting=== Hudgins received no [[NCAA Division I]] offers. He was noticed by [[Northwest Missouri State Bearcats men's basketball|Northwest Missouri State]] head coach [[Ben McCollum]] at an [[Amateur Athletic Union]] tournament game in [[Lawrence, Kansas]], in July 2016. McCollum later travelled to Manhattan to watch Hudgins play pickup basketball at the Ahearn Field House and was satisfied by his aggression; Hudgins received an offer to Northwest the next day. Hudgins made two trips to the Northwest Missouri State campus and committed to the program after the team won its first national title in March 2017. ==College career== ===2017–2018: Redshirt season=== Hudgins redshirted during the 2017–18 season; his decision was due to the feeling that he did not live up to expectations during team practices and he spent time conditioning himself to replace senior [[Justin Pitts]] as the Bearcats' starting [[point guard]]. ===2018–2019: Collegiate debut and first championship=== Hudgins made his collegiate debut on November 4, 2018, against the [[Northern State Wolves]] and scored a team-high 25 points.{{cite web |last1=Wegley |first1=Andrew |title=Northwest men's basketball edges Northern State in overtime thriller |url=https://www.nwmissourinews.com/sports/article_e5d4cd20-dff1-11e8-accd-174b3817d6f2.html |website=Northwest Student Media |access-date=June 24, 2022 |date=November 4, 2018}} Hudgins finished the season with averages of 18.7 points, 5.3 assists and 2.3 rebounds per game.{{cite web |title=MHS alum Trevor Hudgins featured in Sports Illustrated segment |url=https://themercury.com/sports/mhs-alum-trevor-hudgins-featured-in-sports-illustrated-segment/article_35dff6fc-f763-5075-a872-2ac9a5c799cc.html |website=The Mercury |access-date=July 4, 2021 |date=May 7, 2019}} His 203 assists broke the Bearcats' single-season assist record.{{cite web |last1=Peterson |first1=Rick |title=Manhattan product Trevor Hudgins on cusp of milestone for Bearcats |url=https://www.cjonline.com/sports/20200116/manhattan-product-trevor-hudgins-on-cusp-of-milestone-for-bearcats |website=The Topeka Capital-Journal |access-date=July 4, 2021 |date=January 16, 2020}} Hudgins helped lead the Bearcats to a 38–0 record and was selected as the Freshman of the Year in the [[Mid-America Intercollegiate Athletics Association]] (MIAA) while also earning first-team all-MIAA honors. The Bearcats defeated the [[Point Loma Nazarene Sea Lions]] in the championship game of the [[2019 NCAA Division II men's basketball tournament]] with Hudgins scoring 12 points and a game-high six assists. He was named the Division II [[Elite Eight]] Most Outstanding Player.{{cite web |last1=Walker |first1=Jon |title=Hudgins named NABC Division II Player of the Year, becomes second Northwest men's basketball player to earn award |url=https://www.nwmissourinews.com/sports/article_7b0a5f68-8c75-11eb-befe-b353664089bf.html |website=Northwest Missouri News |access-date=July 4, 2021 |date=March 24, 2021}} ===2019–2020: Postseason cancelled=== Hudgins desired to become a greater offensive threat during his redshirt sophomore season of 2019–20.{{cite web |last1=Kraft |first1=Tyler |title=MHS alum Trevor Hudgins searching for path forward after canceled season |url=https://themercury.com/sports/mhs-alum-trevor-hudgins-searching-for-path-forward-after-canceled-season/article_5bac23f0-cfe3-5b27-8c61-914e41c3bb24.html |website=The Mercury |access-date=July 4, 2021 |date=May 31, 2020}} He averaged 19.6 points and 6 assists per game as he helped the Bearcats to achieve a 31–1 record. The Bearcats won the MIAA tournament for the second consecutive year and were poised to be the No. 1 seed in the [[2020 NCAA Division II men's basketball tournament]] until its cancellation due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]]. Hudgins was honored as the MIAA Player of the Year and selected to the All-MIAA First-Team.{{cite web |title=MIAA Announces 2020 Men’s Basketball Postseason Awards, Teams |url=https://themiaa.com/news/2020/3/3/miaa-announces-2020-mens-basketball-postseason-awards-teams.aspx |website=Mid-America Intercollegiate Athletics Association |access-date=July 4, 2021 |date=March 3, 2020}} He was selected as a finalist for the [[Bevo Francis Award]] alongside teammate [[Ryan Hawkins]].{{cite web |last1=Martin |first1=Derek |title=Northwest's Hawkins, Hudgins named finalists for 2020 Bevo Francis Award |url=https://www.kmaland.com/sports/northwests-hawkins-hudgins-named-finalists-for-2020-bevo-francis-award/article_4ea385e2-76b6-11ea-99b2-c73a6b5ca4ee.html |website=KMA Land |access-date=July 4, 2021 |date=April 4, 2020}} ===2020–2021: National prominence and second championship=== Hudgins averaged 19.8 points and 4.6 assists during the 2020–21 season; his 3.16 assist-to-turnover ratio was second-best amongst all [[National Collegiate Athletic Association]] (NCAA) players. The Bearcats achieved a 28–2 record and defeated the [[West Texas A&M Buffaloes]] in the [[2021 NCAA Division II men's basketball tournament]] for Hudgins to win his second national championship.{{cite web |last1=Kinley |first1=Glenn |title=Trevor Hudgins, Northwest Missouri State, national champions again |url=https://www.ksnt.com/sports/trevor-hudgins-northwest-missouri-state-national-champions-again/ |website=KSNT |access-date=July 4, 2021 |date=March 28, 2021}} He was selected as the MIAA Player of the Year for a second consecutive season and chosen to the All-MIAA First Team for a third straight year. Hudgins did not consider transferring and elected to return to the Bearcats for his senior year during the 2021–22 season.{{cite web |last1=Givony |first1=Jonathan |title=Div. II POY Trevor Hudgins returning to Northwest Missouri State for senior year |url=https://www.espn.com.au/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/31264101/div-ii-poy-trevor-hudgins-returning-northwest-missouri-state-senior-year |website=ESPN |access-date=July 4, 2021 |date=April 16, 2021}}{{cite web |last1=Dykstra |first1=Jon |title=ESPN surprises Hudgins with transfer question |url=http://www.maryvilleforum.com/sports/maryville/espn-surprises-hudgins-with-transfer-question/article_67683d46-a07e-11eb-993a-334b7248f338.html |website=Maryville Forum |access-date=July 4, 2021 |date=April 18, 2021}} He said of his decision: "My coach ([[Ben McCollum]]) took a chance on me when not a lot of teams did. He believed in me and that's my reason for going back to try and win another national championship." He was an early entrant for the [[2021 NBA draft]] but withdrew before it took place.{{cite web |title=NBA announces 88 early entry candidates withdraw from 2021 Draft |url=https://www.nba.com/news/early-entry-candidates-withdraw-draft-2021 |website=NBA.com |access-date=July 28, 2021 |date=July 11, 2021}} ===2021–2022: Final season and third championship=== The Bearcats won the 2022 MIAA Tournament title by defeating Washburn; Hudgins scored 35 points and was selected as the MIAA Tournament Most Outstanding Player.{{cite web |last1=Kinley |first1=Glenn |title=Trevor Hudgins explodes to lead Northwest past Washburn in title game |url=https://www.ksnt.com/sports/washburn-ichabods/trevor-hudgins-explodes-to-lead-northwest-past-washburn-in-title-game/ |website=KSNT |access-date=June 24, 2022 |date=March 6, 2022}} The Bearcats defeated Augusta in the NCAA Division II championship game on March 26, 2022, to win a third consecutive national championship.{{cite web |title=NW Missouri St. beats Augusta for 3rd straight D-II title |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/nw-missouri-st-beats-augusta-220706841.html |website=Yahoo! |access-date=June 24, 2022 |date=March 27, 2022}} Hudgins scored 31 points and became the all-time leader scoring in MIAA history.{{cite web |last1=Kinley |first1=Glenn |title=Trevor Hudgins wins third national title at Northwest Mo. |url=https://www.ksnt.com/sports/local-sports/trevor-hudgins-wins-third-national-title-at-northwest-mo/ |website=KSNT |access-date=June 24, 2022 |date=March 26, 2022}} He earned the NABC Division II Player of the Year award for a second consecutive season.{{cite web |last1=Dea |first1=Micaela |title=Hudgins earns NABC National Player of the Year for second straight season |url=https://www.newspressnow.com/sports/college/northwest_missouri_state_bearcats/hudgins-earns-nabc-national-player-of-the-year-for-second-straight-season/article_ff3bdb36-aadd-11ec-ad7e-4f5bf88dbf50.html |website=News-Press NOW |access-date=June 24, 2022 |date=March 23, 2022}} He won the 2022 [[Bevo Francis Award]] for the best small college basketball player and became the second Northwest Missouri State player to earn the award after Justin Pitts.{{cite web |last1=Roush |first1=Chris |title=Northwest's Trevor Hudgins wins Bevo Francis award for best small college basketball player |url=https://www.kq2.com/sports/northwests-trevor-hudgins-wins-bevo-francis-award-for-best-small-college-basketball-player/article_c73b404c-b487-11ec-935d-1f8970e3418b.html |website=KQ2 |access-date=June 24, 2022 |date=April 4, 2022}} Hudgins declared for the [[2022 NBA draft]].{{cite web |title=24 early-entry candidates withdraw from NBA Draft 2022 |url=https://www.nba.com/news/24-early-entry-candidates-withdraw-from-nba-draft-2022 |website=NBA |access-date=June 24, 2022 |date=June 16, 2022}} He had another year of eligibility available for the 2022–23 season but he planned to graduate and begin his professional career in 2022. Hudgins' strengths in deep range shooting, ability to shoot off the dribble and proficient playing style earned him attention from [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) scouts and a strong senior year was expected to put him in contention for NBA workouts after he graduated. He left Northwest Missouri State as the most decorated player in Division II history.{{cite web |last1=Dykstra |first1=Jon |title=Hudgins, Hawkins prepare for Thursday’s NBA Draft |url=http://www.maryvilleforum.com/sports/hudgins-hawkins-prepare-for-thursday-s-nba-draft/article_c4201fc8-f13a-11ec-a8a7-7b11b22df1f7.html |website=Maryville Forum |access-date=June 24, 2022 |date=June 21, 2022}} McCollum called Hudgins "the best player in Division II history."{{cite web |last1=Walker |first1=Jon |title=Meet Trevor Hudgins: 'The best player in Division II history' |url=https://www.nwmissourinews.com/sports/article_5470d70e-c0e7-11ec-9244-e781f715fe05.html |website=Northwest Student Media |access-date=June 24, 2022 |date=April 21, 2022}} ==Professional career== ===Houston Rockets (2022–2023)=== Hudgins worked out for the [[Brooklyn Nets]] and [[Houston Rockets]] prior to the [[2022 NBA draft]]. After going undrafted, he signed a [[two-way contract]] with the Rockets on July 1 and became the first player from [[Northwest Missouri State University|Northwest Missouri State]] to sign an NBA contract.{{cite web|title=Rockets Sign Trevor Hudgins to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-sign-trevor-hudgins-to-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=July 1, 2022|access-date=July 1, 2022}}{{cite web|first=Cody|last=Taylor|title=Rockets sign Division II star Trevor Hudgins to two-way contract|url=https://therookiewire.usatoday.com/2022/07/03/rockets-trevor-hudgins-two-way-contract/|website=USAToday.com|date=July 3, 2022|access-date=July 7, 2022}} Hudgins played for the Rockets in the [[2022 NBA Summer League]] and averaged 5.4 points per game.{{cite web|first=Coty|last=Davis|title=Rockets Summer League Player Recaps: Aric Holman, Trevor Hudgins, Trhae Mitchell|url=https://www.si.com/nba/rockets/news/houston-summer-league-player-recaps-aric-holman-trevor-hudgins-trhae-mitchell|website=SI.com|date=July 19, 2022|access-date=July 26, 2022}} He made his regular season debut for the Rockets on October 22, 2022, as he scored 3 points in a loss to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].{{cite web|title=Former MHS star Hudgins records 1st NBA basket|url=https://themercury.com/sports/former-mhs-star-hudgins-records-1st-nba-basket/article_082caab9-ce3a-5d6a-aa79-eede3fd2f384.html|work=Manhattan Mercury|date=October 22, 2022|access-date=October 29, 2022}} Hudgins made four other appearances in a three-week stretch in February 2023 due to starters [[Kevin Porter Jr.]] and [[Jalen Green]] being out of the line-up.{{cite web|title=Rockets' Trevor Hudgins: Rocky rookie season|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/rockets-trevor-hudgins-rocky-rookie-season/|website=CBSSports.com|date=April 13, 2023|access-date=April 15, 2023}} He averaged 1.8 points and .6 assists in 5 games with the Rockets. Hudgins primarily spent his rookie season with the [[Rio Grande Valley Vipers]] of the [[NBA G League]] where he averaged 20 points, 6.1 assists and 2.5 rebounds per game. On July 2, 2023, Hudgins signed a second two-way contract with the Rockets,{{cite web|first=Jerald|last=Rogers|title=Rockets Re-Sign Darius Days and Trevor Hudgins to Two-Way Contracts|url=https://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-re-sign-darius-days-and-trevor-hudgins-to-two-way-contracts|website=NBA.com|date=July 2, 2023|access-date=July 2, 2023}} but was waived on October 23.{{cite web|first=Hiren|last=Joshi|title=Rockets Sign Nate Hinton to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-sign-nate-hinton-to-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=October 23, 2023|access-date=October 30, 2023}} ===Le Mans (2023–2026)=== On November 7, 2023, Hudgins signed with [[Le Mans Sarthe Basket|Le Mans]] of the [[LNB Pro A]] to replace [[Nate Mason]].{{cite web|title=Le MSB officialise le renfort du meneur Trevor Hudgins|url=https://www.msb.fr/index.php/component/content/article/119-equipes/pros/recrutement/5911-le-msb-officialise-le-renfort-du-meneur-trevor-hudgins?Itemid=101|website=MSB.fr|date=November 7, 2023|access-date=November 7, 2023|language=French}} He averaged 12.6 points and 2.9 assists per game during the 2023–24 season.{{cite web |last1=Dykstra |first1=Jon |title=Hudgins returns from France ready for opportunity with Clippers |url=https://www.maryvilleforum.com/sports/hudgins-returns-from-france-ready-for-opportunity-with-clippers/article_2e626b3a-3f0d-11ef-9596-b7fab328854b.html |website=Maryville Forum |access-date=August 12, 2024 |date=July 10, 2024}} Hudgins played for the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] during the [[2024 NBA Summer League]]. On July 22, 2024, Hudgins re-signed with Le Mans for the 2024–25 season.{{cite web |title=Trevoir Hudgins complète l'effectif du MSB version 2024-2025 |url=https://www.msb.fr/index.php/component/content/article/119-equipes/pros/recrutement/6086-trevoir-hudgins-complete-l-effectif-du-msb-version-2024-2025?Itemid=101 |website=MSB.fr |access-date=August 12, 2024 |language=French |date=July 22, 2024}} He averaged 16.0 points, 1.8 rebounds and 2.9 assists and was selected to the All-[[LNB Élite]] Second Team.{{cite web |last1=Puybertier |first1=Arthur |title=Le second cinq de la saison de Betclic ÉLITE dévoilé |url=https://www.bebasket.fr/le-second-cinq-de-la-saison-de-betclic-elite-devoile |website=BeBasket |access-date=May 28, 2025 |language=French |date=May 15, 2025}} Hudgins was selected to the All-[[LNB Élite]] Second Team for a second consecutive season in 2026 after he averaged 15.7 points and 3.9 assists per game.{{cite web |last1=Cuvelliez |first1=Hugo |title=Adam Mokoka, seul Français du deuxième cinq de la saison de Betclic ÉLITE |url=https://www.bebasket.fr/adam-mokoka-seul-francais-du-deuxieme-cinq-de-la-saison-de-betclic-elite |website=BeBasket |access-date=June 8, 2026 |language=French |date=May 14, 2026}} ===PAOK
